title: Department of Justice, Ministry of Law and Justice organises Regional Workshop in Goa under DISHA 2.0 Scheme
subtitle:
Union Minister of State (Independent change) for Law and Justice Arjun Ram Meghwal highlights importance of Tele-Law and Pro Bono Legal Services in strengthening Access to Justice

Chief Guest -Shri Pusapati Ashok Gajapathi Raju, Governor of Goa underscores access to justice is central to the constitutional vision of ensuring dignity, fairness and equal opportunity for every citizen, irrespective of social or economic background
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                21 SEP 2026 3:33PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The Department of Justice, Ministry of Law and Justice, Government of India, organised a Regional Workshop under the DISHA 2.0 Scheme on 21 September 2026 in India International University of Legal Education and Research (IIULER) Goa. The workshop brought together key stakeholders associated with access to justice, legal awareness, legal aid and technology-enabled legal services, with a focus on strengthening citizen-centric justice delivery and enhancing awareness of legal rights and remedies.
The Regional Workshop highlighted the initiatives being undertaken by the Department of Justice under DISHA 2.0 Scheme, including the use of technology and community-based mechanisms to facilitate access to legal information, advice and assistance. The programme also provided a platform for interaction among beneficiaries, Village Level Entrepreneurs (VLEs), and Panel Lawyers, showcasing their experiences and role in taking legal services closer to citizens.
The programme was graced by the Governor of Goa, Pusapati Ashok Gajapathi Raju as the Chief Guest, along with  Minister of State (Independent Charge) for Law and Justice, Government of India Arjun Ram Meghwal, and Prof. (Dr.) R. Venkata Rao, Vice-Chancellor, India International University of Legal Education and Research, Goa.  The event brought together officials from the Central Government and Government of Goa, representatives of Common Service Centres (CSCs), law institutions of Goa State and other stakeholders working towards ensuring accessible and inclusive justice delivery.
In his welcome address, Shri Suresh Kumar, Joint Secretary, Department of Justice, Ministry of Law and Justice welcomed the dignitaries and participants. He highlighted the Department of Justice’s commitment to strengthening access to justice through DISHA 2.0 Scheme, with its focus on Tele-Law, Nyaya Bandhu, Legal Literacy and Legal Awareness Programme, and VIDHI-Sanjeevani. He also highlighted the “Nyaya Prabodh” initiatives, including “Know Your Rights in 90 Seconds” and the Slogan Competition, along with the documentary and interactions showcasing the implementation of DISHA 2.0 Scheme in Goa. He appreciated the pro bono legal work undertaken by law colleges under Nyaya Bandhu and emphasized that legal awareness, technology-enabled justice delivery and community participation are central to ensuring inclusive and citizen-centric access to justice.
A major highlight of the workshop was the showcase of the best five reels received and shortlisted under the “Know Your Rights in 90 Seconds” campaign, being undertaken as part of “Nyaya Prabodh – Awakening to Justice”. The event also marked the launch of a Slogan Competition under the Nyaya Prabodh campaign, with the aim to deepen citizens’ understanding of their constitutional and legal rights, promote legal literacy, and foster greater public engagement and participation in the Justice delivery ecosystem. Participants are invited to submit their slogans till 31st December 2026 on Department of Justice’s website https://www.doj.gov.in.
A documentary highlighting the implementation and outreach of DISHA Scheme in Goa was screened during the programme. The programme was followed by a live interaction with beneficiaries of the Scheme, VLEs, and Panel Lawyers, providing an opportunity to share experiences relating to the delivery of legal advice and assistance through DISHA 2.0 initiatives.
The workshop also featured an interaction with student and faculty of the Law School under Nyaya Bandhu (Pro Bono Legal services) in Goa, highlighting the role of the legal fraternity and educational institutions in promoting pro bono legal services and contributing to the objective of access to justice for all.
Prof. (Dr.) R. Venkata Rao Hon'ble Vice-Chancellor, India International University of Legal Education and Research, Goa, in his address stated that it was a momentous day for IIULER, Goa, as the institution was collaborating with the Pro Bono Club Scheme under the DISHA 2.0 Scheme of the Department of Justice, Ministry of Law & Justice. He appreciated DISHA Scheme for providing effective tools and platforms to advance access to justice and emphasised that pro bono lawyering is an essential responsibility for young lawyers. He appreciated the Nyaya Setu AI Chatbot launched by the Department of Justice under the DISHA Scheme as an important initiative for enabling citizens to access legal information and assistance.
Hon’ble Minister of State (I/C) for Law & Justice, Shri Arjun Ram Meghwal highlighted that access to justice is not limited to courts and legal processes, but also involves empowering citizens with knowledge of their rights and ensuring that legal information and services are simple, accessible and responsive. Highlighting the significance of pro bono service, he referred to the inspiring legacy of Chittaranjan Das and Shri Arvind Ghosh in the historic Alipur Dwar Case before the Calcutta High Court, where C.R. Das selflessly appeared to defend Shri Arvind Ghosh and powerfully argued for justice, leading to his acquittal. He noted that this spirit of service continues through the Nyaya Bandhu initiative and described pro bono advocates as playing a role akin to guardians of justice. He also emphasized the importance of legal awareness initiatives under “Nyaya Prabodh: Awakening to Justice”, particularly in engaging educational institutions, students and young professionals in promoting legal literacy and a culture of service.
In his keynote address, Hon’ble Governor of Goa, Shri Pusapati Ashok Gajapathi Raju underscored that access to justice is central to the constitutional vision of ensuring dignity, fairness and equal opportunity for every citizen, irrespective of social or economic background. He highlighted the importance of legal awareness and citizen empowerment in enabling people to understand their rights, seek timely assistance and access appropriate remedies. Referring to the “Nyaya Prabodh: Awakening to Justice” initiative, he noted that an informed citizen is an empowered citizen and appreciated the participation of students, educational institutions and young professionals in strengthening legal literacy and the rule of law. He further emphasized that access to justice is a shared responsibility of Governments, Courts, Legal professionals, Academia, Civil Society and citizens, and called for collective efforts to build a more accessible, responsive and humane justice delivery ecosystem towards the vision of Viksit Bharat @2047.
The workshop concluded with the presentation of mementos to the guests and the Vote of Thanks by Director, Department of Justice. The programme concluded with the National Song followed by the National Anthem.
The Regional Workshop reaffirmed the Department of Justice’s continued efforts under DISHA 2.0 Scheme towards strengthening legal literacy, facilitating access to legal services, promoting pro bono engagement and leveraging technology and community-level outreach mechanisms to ensure that the benefits of justice delivery reach citizens across the country.

title: Ministry of MSME Gears Up for Special Campaign 6.0 on Swachhata and Disposal of Pendency
subtitle: Ministry has disposed 22,365 Public Grievances and Freed 1,167 Sq. Ft. Space under Special Campaign 5.0
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                21 SEP 2026 3:30PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The Ministry of Micro, Small & Medium Enterprises (MSME) is gearing up for Special Campaign 6.0, to be conducted from 2nd to 31st October, 2026 under the aegis of the Department of Administrative Reforms & Public Grievances (DARPG). The Campaign seeks to improve cleanliness and citizen experience across Government offices, with this edition placing added emphasis on “effective collection, segregation and disposal of e-waste” in line with the E-Waste (Management) Rules, 2022, and on field/outstation offices that directly interface with the public, besides Ministries/Departments, their attached and subordinate offices, Autonomous Bodies and PSUs.
A Preparatory Phase (15–30 September, 2026) is currently underway, during which the Ministry is sensitizing offices down to the field level, and drawing up an action plan for the campaign. The subsequent Implementation Phase (2–31 October, 2026) will drive cleanliness, e-waste disposal, digitisation, record weeding, space management, and clearance of pending MP References, State Government references, Parliamentary Assurances, PMO references, and public grievances.
In Special Campaign 5.0, the Ministry and its organisations — the Office of the Development Commissioner (MSME), Khadi & Village Industries Commission, Coir Board, National Small Industries Corporation, National Institute for Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises, and Mahatma Gandhi Institute for Rural Industrialisation — reviewed 23,162 physical files, weeded out 4,280 files, freed up 21,045 sq. ft. of office space, and disposed of scrap worth ₹22.89 lakh. Over 81% of MP references and 99% of public grievances were cleared, as part of 1,045 cleanliness campaigns conducted during the period.
Further, pursuant to DARPG’s directions to sustain the momentum generated under Special Campaign 5.0, Ministry directed its organisations to undertake activities on various parameters of the Campaign. As a result, during the period from November, 2025 to September 2026, 22,365 Public Grievances, 4850 Public Grievances Appeals, 226 MP references have been disposed; 626 Physical files and 127 E-files have been weeded out after review and around 1167 sq ft. of space has been freed. Moreover, officers of the Ministry have visited its field offices and institutions, to sensitise the staff, and review their performance in the Campaign.

Building on these gains, the Ministry and its organisations remain committed to carry Special Campaign 6.0 forward with the same rigour, towards cleaner and more responsive governance.

Union Minister for Coal and Mines, Shri G. Kishan Reddy, today inaugurated the National Seminar on “India’s Critical Minerals Recycling Ecosystem and Circular Economy”, organised by the Ministry of Mines, Government of India, in collaboration with the Materials Recycling Association of India (MRAI), at Hyatt Regency, New Delhi.
The day-long seminar brought together policymakers, industry leaders, recyclers, experts, researchers, academia and other stakeholders to deliberate on strengthening India’s critical minerals recycling ecosystem and advancing a circular economy.
In his keynote address, Shri G. Kishan Reddy highlighted the strategic importance of critical minerals recycling for India’s clean energy transition, defence preparedness, digital economy and advanced manufacturing. He called for greater collaboration among government, industry, research institutions and startups to promote the recovery of critical minerals from End-of-Life (EOL) products and strengthen domestic recycling capabilities.
The Minister emphasised the need for innovative technologies, entrepreneurship, responsible e-waste management and environmental sustainability. Underscoring the importance of Jan Bhagidari, he urged citizens to view e-waste and EOL products as valuable resources for critical mineral recovery. He also called upon industry, companies and researchers to share ideas and work collectively towards a technology-driven and sustainable recycling ecosystem in line with the vision of Viksit Bharat.
Minister of State for Coal and Mines, Shri Satish Chandra Dubey, highlighted the importance of strengthening critical minerals recovery and recycling capabilities to promote resource efficiency and build a circular and self-reliant ecosystem. He stressed the need to take awareness on responsible waste management and e-waste recycling to the grassroots through wider public participation and village-to-village outreach, ensuring that recyclable resources are channelled into the formal recycling ecosystem.
Secretary, Ministry of Mines, Shri Keshav Chandra, underlined the strategic importance of critical minerals for clean energy technologies, advanced manufacturing, electronics, defence and other strategic sectors. He emphasised the need for a robust domestic ecosystem covering exploration, processing, recovery and recycling.
Shri Keshav Chandra noted that e-waste, industrial waste and other EOL materials can serve as important secondary sources for recovering critical minerals, thereby improving resource efficiency, reducing dependence on primary sources and supporting a circular economy. He called for coordinated and time-bound action by stakeholders, with clear responsibilities and defined timelines, to strengthen India’s critical mineral security.
During the seminar, the Union MinisterS also launched the Concept Paper on Critical Mineral Recycling Ecosystem, which outlines a strategic framework for strengthening critical mineral recycling in India, with a focus on resource efficiency, recovery from secondary sources and development of a circular and self-reliant ecosystem.
The seminar featured technical sessions on critical mineral recycling and e-waste collection; lithium-ion battery metal recovery and export of black mass; non-ferrous metals recycling; and the critical minerals and non-ferrous metals recycling landscape. The discussions covered technological advancements, R&D, e-waste collection, recovery of critical minerals from lithium-ion batteries and other EOL materials, black mass processing, and policy measures for strengthening the recycling sector.
The Ministry of Mines is also giving focused attention to responsible e-waste management and recycling as part of its broader efforts towards sustainable resource use. In the context of Special Campaign 6.0 and Swachhata Hi Seva, the Ministry is promoting awareness, responsible disposal and channelisation of e-waste into the formal recycling ecosystem. These efforts complement the Ministry’s broader focus on circular economy, resource efficiency and sustainable management of valuable materials, including critical minerals.

title: Solar Energy Corporation of India Limited will continue to play a central role towards achievement of India’s clean energy vision: Shri Shripad Yesso Naik

content:
“SECI's 15-year journey stands as a reflection of India's growing leadership in the global renewable energy transition,” said Shri Shripad Yesso Naik, Minister of State, Ministry of New & Renewable Energy and Power while addressing the gathering at the celebration of the 15th Foundation Day of Solar Energy Corporation of India Limited (SECI) here today as the Chief Guest.
Shri Naik said that SECI has consistently delivered on the nation’s clean energy vision and expressed confidence that the corporation will continue to play a central role towards its achievement.
The event was also graced by Shri Ghanshyam Prasad, Chairperson, CEA, Shri Mayank Tewari, Additional Secretary, MNRE and Shri Vivek Jain, Chairman, INOXGFL Group along with other senior officials of the Renewable Energy sector.
Speaking at the event, Shri Akash Tripathi, Managing Director, SECI, said that SECI remains committed to open new opportunities in the renewable energy sector, working closely with all stakeholders and innovating with market's requirements. These 15 years have been a testament to SECI's dedication and the nation's collective will towards sustainable energy. We are thankful to all our stakeholders for putting their faith in us.
The Stakeholders’ Meet featured two thematic sessions, “Reimagining Industry through Green Molecules” and “The Changing Energy Landscape: Distributed Renewables and New Energy Markets,” bringing together policymakers, industry leaders and financial institutions to deliberate on emerging opportunities and challenges shaping India’s energy transition.
The first session, “Reimagining Industry through Green Molecules,” explored the role of green hydrogen and its derivatives in decarbonising hard-to-abate sectors and creating new avenues for industrial growth. The session covered opportunities for domestic production and emerging applications, along with the policy support, infrastructure, technology and financing required to develop green molecule markets on a scale.
The second session, “The Changing Energy Landscape: Distributed Renewables and New Energy Markets,” examined the evolving role of distributed RE in India. Key areas of discussion included greater consumer participation, integration of distributed energy resources and emerging market mechanisms, as well as the policy and regulatory frameworks needed to facilitate their effective integration and support the expansion of renewable energy.
As SECI marks 15 years of service to the nation, its cumulative achievements stand at over 41 GW of renewable energy generation capacity commissioned through third-party developers, power sale agreements of over 67 GW signed with various DISCOMs/consumers, and cumulative market investments enabled for about ₹3.6 lakh crores. The company is rapidly scaling with its own projects' portfolio as well and is also active in promoting energy storage, green hydrogen and allied areas.
Incorporated on September 20, 2011, SECI, a Navratna CPSE under the Ministry of New and Renewable Energy, began as the country's dedicated implementing agency for the National Solar Mission and has since grown into the foremost CPSE focused exclusively on Renewable Energy, with a mandate spanning the complete Renewable Energy ecosystem.

title: Preparations Underway for Special Campaign 6 for Institutionalizing Swachhata and Disposal of Pending Matters over Indian Railways
subtitle:
Focus on E-Waste Disposal, Scrap Disposal, Space Management and Clearance of Pending References

Over 150 Nodal Officers Designated for Monitoring and Coordinating Campaign Activities
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                21 SEP 2026 1:32PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Special Campaign 6 for institutionalizing Swachhata and minimizing pendency in Government offices has been launched by the Government of India. The campaign is structured into two phases: the Preparatory Phase from 15th to 30th September 2026 for setting targets, followed by the main Implementation Phase from 2nd to 31 October 2026.
During the previous Campaign 5.0, the Ministry of Railways demonstrated significant progress by achieving 100% of the identified targets pertaining to disposal of public grievances, VIP references, and other pending matters. Remarkable achievements included the release of 6.06 lakh square feet of space and the generation of revenue amounting to ₹570 Crore.
The Ministry of Railways is fully prepared for the successful implementation of the Special Campaign for Disposal of Pending Matters 6 (SCDPM 6) across all its field units, attached and subordinate offices, PSUs, and autonomous bodies. The Railway Board is closely monitoring the preparations to accord highest priority to the campaign. Detailed guidelines from the Department of Administrative Reforms And Public Grievances (DARPG) have been communicated to all field units to mobilize ground functionaries, identify campaign sites, and plan for space management. A D.O. letter from the Secretary, Railway Board, to all General Managers and Heads of other Units has also been issued in this regard.
Detailed instructions have been issued to all Zonal Railways, Divisional Offices, Public Sector Undertakings (PSUs), Production Units (PUs), and Central Training Institutes to ensure saturation-level participation. More than 150 nodal officers have been designated across Indian Railways to coordinate the effort and will collect progress information on a daily basis and will send it to the Railway Board enabling it to feed directly into DARPG's central SCDPM monitoring portal, facilitating real-time tracking and weekly high-level reviews.
As the preparatory phase is now underway, targets are being finalized with respect to key campaign parameters. In line with this year's focus, special emphasis is placed on "Effective Collection, Segregation, and Disposal of E-Waste" as per E-Waste (Management) Rules, 2022, scrap disposal under General Financial Rules (GFR), office space beautification, process/rule simplification and including clearance of pending references.
Following the successful organisation of Rail Chaupal (SCDPM 4.0) and Amrit Samvaad (SCDPM 5.0), the Ministry will organise “Rail Jan Samvaad” during SCDPM 6 to further strengthen public engagement and foster meaningful dialogue with citizens.
Reaffirming its commitment to embedding cleanliness as a routine operational standard, the Ministry of Railways continues to prioritize seamless public engagement and the prompt disposal of pending references. With coordinated planning and dedicated participation across all units, the Ministry aims to make Special Campaign 6 a resounding success.

title: NHAI Introduces New Guidelines for Design and Development of Access-Controlled High-Speed National Highways
subtitle: Guidelines establish uniform framework for planning and design, strengthen safety and facilitate seamless movement on High-Speed Corridors
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                21 SEP 2026 4:43PM by PIB Delhi
content:
In line with the Government of India’s vision of Viksit Bharat 2047 and long-term objective of developing a world-class National Highway network, NHAI has released comprehensive guidelines for the planning and designing of High-Speed Access controlled National Highways, other than Expressways.
The guidelines seek to bring uniformity in standards for preparation of Detailed Project Reports (DPRs) of high-speed National Highway corridors and bring greater consistency in technical standards, strengthen road safety, improve operational efficiency across the National Highway network. The guidelines will apply to all upcoming 4/6 lane Greenfield and Brownfield High-speed access controlled National Highways.
Need for uniform standards
The guidelines are aligned with the long-term Government of India’s strategic roadmap which envisages the development of 50,000 km of access-controlled High-Speed Corridors under Viksit Bharat 2047, boosting connectivity and reducing logistics costs.
At present, there are no separate standards and specifications governing planning and designing of access control High-Speed access controlled National Highways, other than Expressways. Variations have been observed in the standards adopted for preparation of DPR for such corridors. The new guidelines address this requirement by providing a uniform set of technical and safety provisions.
A key focus of the guidelines is on incorporation of additional safety measures appropriate with high-speed traffic conditions on corridors. Special provisions have been prescribed for advance notification of exits and entries, enabling National Highway users to anticipate and safely navigate upcoming access and egress points.
Uniform Design Framework for Access-Controlled National Highways
The lane configuration of the High-speed National Highways will be standardized based on detailed traffic assessment. Corridors with traffic-flow up to 15,000 vehicles with four-lane highway & four lane structures will have width of 60 metres. Similarly, corridors having traffic-flow between 15,000 - 25,000 vehicles with four-lane highway & six lane structures will have width of 70 metres. Also, Highways with traffic-flow between 25,000 – 40,000 vehicles will have width of 70 metres for six-lane highway & six-lane structures configuration.
Access Control and Uninterrupted Traffic Movement
Interchanges with ramps will be provided at crossings with Expressways, National Highways, State Highways and important arterial roads generating substantial traffic, as well as roads providing connectivity to major traffic-generating destinations such as ports, airports, Multi-Modal Logistics Parks (MMLPs), industrial areas and major tourist destinations.
To strengthen access control and prevent encroachments, unauthorized access and entry of stray cattle onto High-Speed Corridors, the guidelines prescribe construction of a 1-metre-high boundary wall along the outer edge of the corridor. The comprehensive guidelines represent a significant step towards standardizing planning and design of fully access-controlled National Highways and ensuring consistency across High-Speed National Highway projects.
The initiative reinforces NHAI’s commitment to develop a safe, seamless and future-ready National Highway network, while contributing to the Government of India’s vision of Viksit Bharat 2047.

content:
The National Steering Committee (NSC) of the Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship (MSDE) has approved a Strategic Investment Plan (SIP) worth ₹320 crore for the Kurukshetra ITI Cluster in Haryana under the Pradhan Mantri Skilling and Employability Transformation through Upgraded ITIs (PM-SETU) scheme. Jindal Naveen Avsar Limited will partner with the Government of Haryana as the Anchor Industry Partner for the cluster.
With this approval, the cumulative investment sanctioned under PM-SETU has risen to ₹2,491 crore across 10 ITI clusters, reinforcing the Government’s commitment to transforming Industrial Training Institutes into industry-led, future-ready centres of excellence that are aligned with evolving workforce requirements.
The approval marks another significant step towards strengthening the industry-led transformation of Government Industrial Training Institutes and creating a more demand-driven vocational training ecosystem.
Shri Jayant Chaudhary, Minister of State (Independent Charge), Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship, said: "Bringing industry closer to ITIs will create stronger employment pathways for our youth. The approval of the Kurukshetra cluster under PM-SETU reflects our commitment to making skill development more relevant, aspirational and responsive to the changing needs of industry. Through strong industry partnerships, we are working to ensure that young people are equipped with the skills, exposure and opportunities required to participate meaningfully in India's growth story”.
One Hub and Six Spoke ITIs to be Transformed
The Kurukshetra cluster will be developed under the Hub-and-Spoke model envisaged under PM-SETU and will comprise seven Government ITIs.
Government ITI, Kurukshetra will serve as the Hub ITI, while the following institutes will function as Spoke ITIs:
Government ITI (Women), Kurukshetra
Government ITI, Kaithal
Government ITI (Women), Kaithal
Government ITI, Pehowa
Government ITI, Pabnawa
Government ITI (Women), Ambala City
The ₹320 crore investment will support the development of an integrated and industry-responsive skilling ecosystem across the cluster. The proposed interventions will focus on strengthening infrastructure, modernising training facilities, introducing industry-aligned courses, and enhancing employability outcomes for trainees.
Strengthening Industry-ITI Linkages
Under PM-SETU, industry partners play a central role in shaping the transformation of ITIs through curriculum development, infrastructure enhancement, training delivery, faculty engagement, apprenticeships, industry exposure and placement support. The scheme aims to ensure that vocational training remains aligned with emerging technologies and evolving labour market demands.
As the Anchor Industry Partner, Jindal Naveen Avsar Limited will work closely with the Government of Haryana and the participating ITIs to strengthen industry linkages and improve student access to practical training, apprenticeships and employment opportunities. The company is already associated with the Barbil ITI Cluster in Odisha, where a Strategic Investment Plan of ₹240 crore has been approved under PM-SETU. Its participation in both clusters reflects growing industry confidence in the scheme's vision of industry-led skilling transformation.
About PM-SETU
PM-SETU is a flagship Government of India initiative aimed at enhancing the quality, relevance and outcomes of vocational training through modern infrastructure, upgraded laboratories and equipment, industry-aligned curricula, introduction of courses in emerging sectors, and stronger industry partnerships.
The scheme has a total outlay of ₹60,000 crore and envisages the upgradation of 1,000 Government ITIs through an industry-led Hub-and-Spoke model, comprising 200 Hub ITIs and 800 Spoke ITIs across the country.
In addition, the scheme provides for capacity augmentation of five National Skill Training Institutes (NSTIs), including the establishment of sector-specific National Centres of Excellence and the strengthening of training-of-trainers capabilities, thereby supporting the creation of a robust and future-ready skilling ecosystem.

35,480 candidates

₹
81.34 crore

Although his monthly income later rose to approximately ₹22,500, meeting regular expenses while creating savings for future needs continued to be a challenge. Shri Rao aspired to secure an additional source of income that would help him support his household and plan for emergencies with greater confidence.
On 21 August 2025, Shri Rao and four other members received assistance under the Swachhta Udyami Yojana for a group project involving the procurement of a Gulfer 8 KL desludging vehicle. The total project cost was Rs 50 lakh. Financial support comprised a loan of Rs 31.25 lakh and an upfront capital subsidy of Rs 18.75 lakh. The intervention enabled the group to undertake mechanised sanitation services and develop an additional, sustainable source of livelihood.
Through the project, Shri Rao now earns approximately Rs 10,000 extra per month alongside his regular employment. His total monthly income has consequently increased from approximately Rs 22,500 to Rs 32,500. The additional earnings have reduced financial stress, enabled him to manage household expenses more comfortably and helped him begin saving for future family needs.
Today, Shri Rao is moving towards a more secure and dignified future for his family. title: “Sources and Methods for Compilation of National Accounts Statistics”
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                21 SEP 2026 4:27PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The
New Series of National Accounts Statistics with base year 2022-23
was released by Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI) on
27th February 2026
and subsequently updated on
31st August 2026 to incorporate the changes on account of the new series of PPI (Producer Price Index), IIP (Index of Industrial Production), etc. released in June 2026.
The new series replaces the earlier series with base year 2011-12 and represents the
eighth base year revision of India’s National Accounts Statistics
.
2.         Through this press release, MoSPI is releasing the publication
“Sources and Methods for Compilation of National Accounts Statistics”
. The publication provides a consolidated account of the concepts, definitions, data sources, methodologies and compilation practices exhaustively adopted in the
New Series, and is being brought out in a record time after seven months of the release of the new series.
3.            As part of the process leading to the new series, MoSPI constituted the
Advisory Committee on National Accounts Statistics (ACNAS)
under the Chairmanship of
Professor B.N. Goldar, visiting faculty (Institute of Economic Growth, IEG),
on
27th June 2024 to
deliberate on specific aspects of the base-year revision exercise. ACNAS constituted four sub-committees namely:
(i) Sub-committee for Incorporation of New Data Sources, Rates and Ratios under the Chairmanship of Shri Manish Kumar Sinha (CEO, GSTN); (ii) Sub-committee for Methodological Improvement under the Chairmanship of  Dr. G.C. Manna (Professor, Institute for Human Development); (iii) Sub-committee for Constant Price Estimates under the Chairmanship of Prof B.N. Goldar, (Visiting faculty, IEG); and (iv) Sub-committee on Regional Accounts under the Chairmanship of Prof R. H. Dholakia (Retd. Professor, IIM, Ahmedabad) for  focused discussion in these areas.
The members of ACNAS and its sub-committees comprised of a distinguished and diverse group of eminent academic experts from a wide range of disciplines, including economics, national accounting, statistics, public policy and related fields.
4.         As part of its deliberations, ACNAS held
nine
rounds of meetings, as well as workshops and seminars involving academia, subject-matter experts, Central and State Government Departments, NITI Aayog and various think tanks across the country. In addition, the sub-committees constituted under ACNAS held more than
35
rounds of meetings to deliberate on specific methodological and data-related issues. The Committee,
inter alia
, advised MoSPI on the inclusion of new and improved data sources for strengthening the compilation of National Accounts estimates, the methodology for the compilation and presentation of National Accounts Statistics for economic analysis and policy formulation, and the adoption and implementation of the latest international standards prescribed by the United Nations. Further, three discussion papers detailing the proposed methodological changes under the themes of Production Approach, Expenditure Approach, and Quarterly GDP and Sub-national Accounts were released for broader consultation.
5.         To facilitate stakeholder engagement and obtain valuable feedback, three Data User Conferences were subsequently organised in Mumbai (26 November 2025), New Delhi (23 December 2025), and Chennai (30 January 2026), bringing together a diverse group of experts, academicians, policymakers, and data users. MoSPI also held detailed consultations with the International Monetary Fund (IMF) on various aspects of the base year revision of GDP. Based on the extensive deliberations with stakeholders, the reports on the recommendations of the first three sub-committees and the guidelines for GSDP based on the recommendations of the fourth sub-committee are available in public domain on the website of MoSPI. The methodologies for compilation of new series of National Accounts Statistics recommended in the reports of the Sub-committees have been incorporated in this publication, “
Sources
and Methods for Compilation of National Accounts Statistics”
.
6.         A key theme of this publication is the modernization of estimation methodologies for the corporate, financial, government, and household sectors. In respect of the Non-Financial Private Corporate (NFPC) sector, report highlights detailed use of corporate filings, LLP records, and enhanced company-level information to improve industry classification, measurement of economic activity, and allocation of output across multiple business segments. The data coverage for financial sector has been substantially expanded. For the General Government sector, the changes expanded to institutional coverage, refinement of the treatment of pension payments, and incorporation of the value of housing facilities provided to employees. In the household sector, after evaluating several alternative methodologies, direct estimation from two surveys of MoSPI, namely, Annual Survey of Unincorporated Sector Enterprises (ASUSE) and Periodic Labour Force Survey (PLFS) has been adopted.
7.         The report further features significant improvements in expenditure-side estimates and quarterly GDP compilation. Private Final Consumption Expenditure (PFCE) has adopted the Classification of Individual Consumption According to Purpose (COICOP) 2018 classification framework of UN, supported by more detailed consumption data and administrative sources. Compilation methodologies for industries, such as, construction, agriculture, livestock, forestry and services have also undergone revision to ensure greater consistency in the estimation of economic activity to reflect recent economic realities and improved data availability. For Quarterly National Accounts, the report underlines replacement of the existing benchmarking method with the Proportional Denton approach, increased use of Goods & Services Tax (GST) and other administrative data. Overall, the report lays the methodological foundation for a more robust, transparent, and data-driven national accounting framework that better captures the evolving structure of the Indian economy. The report also includes the methodology for compilation of Supply Use Tables (SUT) and guidelines for Regional Accounts.
8.         This
publication,
inter alia,
brings together the recommendations made in the reports (already available in the public domain) and presents, in a
consolidated and comprehensive manner
, the statistical framework and processes followed in compiling major macroeconomic aggregates in the
New Series of National Accounts Statistics
. These include
Gross Domestic Product (GDP), National Income, Private Final Consumption Expenditure (PFCE), Gross Fixed Capital Formation (GFCF) and Savings
. At the end of each chapter, summary of Estimates of Gross Value Added (GVA) for the year 2022-23 as per the 2011-12 series and 2022-23 series at current prices have been included as a ready reckoner and for ease of reference. This data is already available in the public domain and no new data is included.
9.         MoSPI gratefully acknowledges the valuable guidance and contributions of the Advisory Committee on National Accounts Statistics (ACNAS) and its various Sub-committees and expert members whose insights and recommendations have enriched this publication. We also extend our sincere appreciation to the Central Ministries and Departments, State Governments, Union Territory Administrations, regulatory bodies, and other stakeholder institutions for their continuous support, cooperation, and provision of critical data and inputs that made this exercise possible.
10.       The
publication
is expected to serve as a comprehensive reference document for
policymakers, researchers, analysts, academics and other users
of National Accounts Statistics for promoting a better understanding of the National Accounts compilation framework.

title: Reclaiming the Land Beneath the Waste
subtitle: Transforming India’s Legacy Dumpsites
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                21 SEP 2026 5:03PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Behind every clean street in urban India lies a chain of infrastructure and systems that manage the waste generated by cities. Every large Indian city generates waste that comes from households, markets, institutions, commercial establishments and public spaces. Much of this waste is directed to dumpsites, where it accumulates over time and forms legacy waste sites. To tackle this challenge, the Swachh Bharat Mission-Urban (SBM-U) was launched in October 2014.
Over 12 years, SBM-U has been building infrastructure beyond basic sanitation. Its focus now extends to managing urban waste and creating better spaces for cities to live, work and gather. Under the Swachh Bharat Mission-Urban 2.0, launched in October 2021, cities across India are undertaking the transformation of legacy dumpsites into productive and environmentally sustainable spaces. The scale of this effort is reflected in the 3.66 crore metric tonnes of legacy waste remediated between January and December 2025. During this time, 459 Urban Local Bodies across 29 States achieved complete dumpsite remediation. The Lakshya Zero Dumpsite initiative under this mission is driving a structured and time-bound effort to scientifically remediate such sites across States and Urban Local Bodies.
Gorakhpur
In Gorakhpur, Uttar Pradesh, a 40-acre site once stood as a towering mound of accumulated municipal waste. For seven years, it served as the city’s primary waste disposal site. The growing waste mound affected the surrounding environment and created difficult living conditions for nearby residents. The site was scientifically remediated through biomining, with around 400 tonnes of waste processed every day. The process separated the accumulated waste into refuse-derived fuel, black soil, recyclables and inert material. Recovered black soil was used for filling low-lying areas, while refuse-derived fuel went to cement industries for co-processing. Gradually, the waste mound gave way to reclaimed land.
Image 1: Dumpsite in Gorakhpur, Uttar Pradesh
The transformation continued beyond clearing the accumulated waste. The entire 40-acre site was developed into the
Kachre Se Kanchan Rapti Eco Park
. The new public space now includes green lawns, walking and jogging tracks, and a children’s play area. An open gym, yoga zone, solar lighting and water conservation structures further expand its public use. Food courts, parking facilities and other amenities have also been incorporated into the park. Several installations made from recycled waste materials highlight the possibilities of resource recovery. The park has also created space for local livelihoods. The women-led self-help group
Shakti Ki Rasoi
operates a restaurant within the park. Today, the park attracts around 500 visitors each day. A site once defined by accumulated waste has thus become a space for recreation and community life.
Delhi
Gorakhpur is not an isolated success. In the national capital, another towering mound is steadily shrinking. The Bhalswa dumpsite, spread over about 70 acres, once held vast quantities of legacy waste. Since July 2022, biomining has been carried out in mission mode continuously at the site.
Image 2: Dumpsite in Bhalswa, Delhi
In September 2025, the annual Swachhata Hi Seva cleanliness campaign was launched nationally from Bhalswa. The site was taken up for accelerated remediation. In November 2025, the Dumpsite Remediation Accelerator Programme (DRAP) was launched. This nationwide, mission-mode initiative fast-tracks the remediation of remaining dumpsites under Swachh Bharat Mission-Urban 2.0.
As part of DRAP, results are now visible in Bhalswa. By May 2026, more than half of the site had been reclaimed, and by 31 July 2026, 99.07 lakh metric tonnes of legacy waste had been remediated.
The work goes beyond removing old waste. Fire-prevention measures, leachate management and other environmental safeguards support safety around the site. Newly awarded work to process fresh waste at the landfill is also being expedited. The goal is to prevent new legacy waste from building up again.
Nagpur
In Nagpur, the Bhandewadi dumping yard is being reshaped into a working waste-processing facility. As a rapidly growing city of over 30 lakh people, Nagpur generates waste from homes, markets, institutions, and public spaces. A significant share of waste used to go to the Bhandewadi dumping yard, which became a major legacy waste site over time.
The city chose to move from open dumping to scientific waste management. Legacy waste was excavated, segregated, and processed in a systematic way. More than 10 lakh metric tonnes of accumulated waste have been treated, which has enabled the reclamation of acres of valuable land, once locked under waste.
Image 3: Bhandewadi dumping yard, Nagpur
The story did not end with reclamation. The site is now an Integrated Municipal Solid Waste Processing Facility. Here, materials are recovered, waste is composted and waste-derived fuel is produced. Modern machines process the waste, while real-time monitoring and CCTV keep a close watch. Dust control and leachate treatment help protect the surroundings.
The transformation has brought benefits for the city. Dependence on landfills has fallen markedly. Air, water and soil quality have improved, along with public health in surrounding areas. The city has also added composting plants, modular processing units and construction and demolition waste systems. Here, waste is no longer seen as a liability, but as a resource to be recovered.
Raichur
In Raichur, Karnataka, the reclaimed land is taking a different form, with 35 acres of Yakalaspura dumpsite being transformed through scientific legacy waste remediation. Around 62,252 metric tonnes of waste have been processed, reclaiming nearly 22 acres of urban land.
Image 4: Yakalaspura dumpsite, Raichur, Karnataka
Part of the restored site now supports sustainable land use, including a Miyawaki forest spread across approximately 5-7 acres. It demonstrates how a former dumpsite can be converted into a thriving ecological space. Around 60,000 bamboo and native saplings are being planted to expand green cover, support biodiversity and restore the soil. The plantation began on
5 June 2026
, with the site inaugurated on World Environment Day. The Yakalaspura transformation is more than waste remediation. The initiative is developed around the concept of “Toxic Waste to Ecological Wealth”. It demonstrates how reclaimed dumpsite land can support ecological restoration and sustainable urban
development.
The
Movement
beyond Cleanup
A reclaimed dumpsite is more than recovered land. It represents a changing approach to managing the waste generated by cities. Across Gorakhpur, Delhi, Nagpur and Raichur, the pattern is the same. Waste mountains are excavated, sorted and turned back into usable land.
Machines and plants alone cannot make this last. City Solid Waste Action Plans, tracked progress on the SBM-U portal and annual Swachh Survekshan rankings keep the work on course long after the ribbon is cut. Infrastructure and institutions together turn a one-time cleanup into a lasting system. Swachh Bharat Mission–Urban began with sanitation, but it has grown well beyond it. It is now reshaping how cities reclaim land, restore ecology and build public spaces where people live, work and gather.

title: Office of PSA convenes first ‘State Governments Nodal Officers Meeting’ to strengthen state-level coordination for wider access to Scientific and R&D infrastructure
subtitle:
I-STEM opens pathways for State Universities, institutions and R&D facilities to connect with the National Scientific Ecosystem

I-STEM expands State-level reach with 31,000+ scientific instruments and 4,000 institutions
ministry: Office of Principal Scientific Advisor to GoI
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                21 SEP 2026 9:17PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Dr. (Mrs.) Parvinder Maini, Scientific Secretary, Office of PSA to the Government of India chaired the first “State Governments Nodal Officers Meeting” for the I-STEM Portal on 21st September 2026. The meeting focused on strengthening the participation of State Governments in the
I-STEM
ecosystem and facilitating the onboarding and effective utilisation of publicly funded scientific infrastructure across States.
I-STEM was conceived and supported by the Office of the PSA and launched by the Hon’ble Prime Minister in January 2020. The platform has expanded into a national resource with more than 31,000 scientific instruments across nearly 4,000 institutions and over 65,000 registered users. By improving the utilisation of existing infrastructure, reducing duplication of investments and facilitating access to specialised facilities, I-STEM is strengthening the research and innovation ecosystem across the country. Also, the listing of publicly funded equipment costing above ₹20 lakh on I-STEM, further strengthens the framework for shared access and optimal utilisation of scientific infrastructure.
The meeting brought together State Government Nodal Officers from 23 States and 4 UTs, along with representatives from the Office of the PSA and I-STEM, to discuss mechanisms for integrating State-level universities, research institutions, laboratories and other R&D facilities with the national I-STEM platform. The meeting included an overview of I-STEM, a detailed orientation on the platform, and an interactive discussion with the Nodal Officers.
In her keynote address, Dr. (Mrs.) Parvinder Maini, Scientific Secretary, Office of PSA, highlighted the need to ensure that India’s investments in scientific and R&D infrastructure are discoverable, accessible and optimally utilised. She emphasised the role of Nodal Officers in facilitating institutional onboarding, equipment listing, wider access and effective utilisation of facilities, while addressing practical issues related to coordination and implementation. She also highlighted the importance of initiatives such as One Nation One Subscription (ONOS) in enabling wider access to high-quality scholarly resources and strengthening the research ecosystem. She further underscored that the larger objective should be to ensure that scientific infrastructure and knowledge resources created through public investment are accessible to the wider R&D and innovation ecosystem and deliver greater value to the country.
Dr. Vishal Choudhary, Scientist ‘F’, Office of PSA, provided an overview of the I-STEM Portal, while Dr. Harilal Bhaskar, COO/National Coordinator, I-STEM, conducted the detailed orientation on the platform and its functionalities. The orientation covered the process of onboarding institutions, listing scientific equipment and enabling wider access to publicly funded R&D infrastructure.
The meeting also highlighted the importance of I-STEM for State universities, colleges, technical institutions and emerging innovation ecosystems, particularly where access to specialised scientific infrastructure may be limited. It was also emphasized that all other existing similar portals (like ANALYTICS portal of CSIR) are being integrated with I-STEM through API linkages.
The deliberations and stakeholder interventions underscored the following key priorities:
Strengthening institutional onboarding: Encouraging universities, research institutions and R&D laboratories under State Governments to register on I-STEM as both users and facility providers.
Expanding access: Enabling researchers, startups, MSMEs and industry to discover and access specialised scientific infrastructure available across institutions and States.
Improving utilisation: Promoting wider and more efficient use of existing publicly funded scientific equipment and facilities.
Supporting infrastructure planning: Using the national infrastructure landscape available through I-STEM to inform future investments and minimise duplication.
Strengthening State-level coordination: Enabling State Government Nodal Officers to act as a link between State Governments, their institutions and the national I-STEM ecosystem, supporting onboarding, equipment listing, awareness and effective utilisation.
The meeting concluded with an emphasis on strengthening coordination between State-level R&D infrastructure and the national science, technology and innovation ecosystem. The State Government Nodal Officers were encouraged to facilitate wider adoption of I-STEM within their respective States and address practical issues relating to institutional onboarding, equipment listing, access, utilisation and coordination.
